sentenceIntentions.text: A useful invention can work perfectly and still have no place in the world.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Make technical success coexist with institutional absence
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel surprise that working is insufficient

sentenceIntentions.text: Artificial Impossibility investigates useful projects that technology allows but existing institutions struggle to support.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Name the category of feasible but unsupported projects

sentenceIntentions.text: A preventive service may save money for someone who never pays its developer.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Show preventive value crossing a payer's boundary

sentenceIntentions.text: An open tool may create value precisely because nobody can own the whole advantage.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Explain why openness can undermine exclusive ownership

sentenceIntentions.text: The book follows these gaps through investment, public funding, professional power, and services people share.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Locate recurring barriers across funding and authority

sentenceIntentions.text: Its named patterns help explain why resistance to change is sometimes the wrong diagnosis.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Offer precise patterns instead of vague resistance stories
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Become curious about named mechanisms behind absence

sentenceIntentions.text: A missing invention starts to look like a question about who could afford to make it possible.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Make unseen projects relevant to founders and citizens
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Notice that missing innovations can carry evidence

sentenceIntentions.text: Begin with the missing sponsor, and consider which possible futures never reach a demonstration.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Wonder which feasible futures lack an institutional home
